body.text: Recorded Under the Effect
Gotō: 02:53 swallowed the first round. 03:53~04:14 second round (the singing was delayed a bit). 05:22 topped up again. 05:27 third round.
Gotō: 05:33 to be honest I don't know how much I've taken anymore, because my emotions are already in pieces.
Gotō: "Peace!"
Gotō: 09:29 severe dissociative anesthesia; I can't type properly.
Gotō: 11:13 the dissociation still hasn't receded much.
Gotō: anyway, I've entered the fifth plateau. The aftereffects are severe: one episode of vomiting, plus my legs are wrecked. Much better after some millet porridge.
Gotō: addendum: very itchy. Also my head.
Recorded After the Effect

Gotō: first I want to prove that where I went really was the fifth plateau, so let me compare... In terms of mental effect, I can guarantee this is the most intense I've experienced so far; I understood completely what dissociation means. The aftereffects lasted absurdly long too: dosed on 11.22, and until just now I thought two months had passed, with dissociation still lingering. A few hours ago I looked up at the white ceiling and vaguely saw external hallucinations! For comparison, normally it only takes me three or four days to clear the aftereffects.

Gotō: I started with a baseline dose, then dosed according to the modified version. After the first dose I felt nothing and played on the computer for a while; two hours later, doubting it had any effect, I took a second round and kept gaming and listening to music; by the third dose, two hours in, it had come on, and the dissociation was so strong even the bitter taste of DXM was far weaker. After that dose I stepped onto the third plateau and started walking...
### Chapter 1

Gotō: I listened to music and kept posting shitty little od jokes, not knowing I was nearly on the fourth plateau. When I finished, I suddenly felt spatial sense vanish, so I tried going from sitting to lying on the floor, and found my body had shrunk, pain was gone, and my movements had become unbelievably light. I stood up, put on Miyuki Nakajima's 'Most Beloved', and started swaying alone on the floor.
Gotō: vision was cancelled; this stretch of memory has no visual record, not even black — only a few scattered images of looking at the floor.

Gotō: auditory memory became blurred. Somewhat abstract: for example, when I recall what I heard in those tens of seconds without dissociation, I can recall it fragment by fragment, second by second; with dissociation, every second's memory is mixed together, including the present, and the sounds can't be told apart.

Gotō: I listened maybe three times, not even a quarter of an hour, but I fell into an emotion without knowing it. Listening to the song, I fell into the despair of that time; every sense but hearing was dissociated away.
### Chapter 3

Gotō: I could see external hallucinations. They appeared first as the classic red-green noise, but this noise was too obvious and the colour blocks too large; then as ATD-like external hallucinations, but not covering the walls the way ATD does. This part of the external hallucination was weak, showing up on the ceiling with the lights off as geometric, moving dark shapes.

Gotō: I saw internal hallucinations. Like a dream. Part 1: I recognised this as a concretization of one of my emotions, consistent with the situation, and I could still think. Part 2: the strings recorded the characteristic characters of my real name and my online name, and I realised it might be something like a character-select menu in a game; I 'ejected'. At the same time, behind it there were several similar 'cards', and I realised that 'I' was not 'one' person.

Gotō: Part 3: my interpersonal relations with each person, with no vision here. Part 4: in front of me were personified questions, and I couldn't make out faces. At that point I had lost the cognition of faces and of human shapes. Part 5: at the end, I was interrogated by the questions in Part 4; what the questions were, I forgot on waking. The image was beautiful: a bright light shining on gloomy me.
### Chapter 4

Gotō: on relationships: the modifiers were pulled out, and I could only grasp the basic meaning. My cognition of QQ, WeChat, Bilibili and Tieba became: QQ — conversations with contacts outside pharmacology; WeChat — mostly conversations with contacts inside pharmacology; Bilibili — a community between people; Tieba — the pharmacology posting area.

Gotō: when I looked at the time, I couldn't distinguish the first digit, and the second was hard. So when I looked a second time, I couldn't compare 4? with 5? in size; all I knew was: it's the end of the half hour at 6.
Gotō: language ability definitely still existed. Even after falling into this chaos, I could still say on my feed, 'protect me'.
### Chapter 5

Gotō: after a spell of the confusion of Chapter 3, I felt I wasn't in this world. This room, these relationships, weren't mine. I felt I could stay on the fifth plateau forever. But the receptors had had enough, so after a spell of dizziness I was, as it were, physically flung out.

Gotō: what I can be sure happened next: my father knocked on the door in the morning to call me to eat. I opened my eyes, and an internal hallucination appeared, like a sci-fi movie HUD. My father's portrait (de-faced) and a relationship tagged 'symbiosis' were boxed in a frame. In my mind I chose 'deflect it', and at that point I was still coming down off the fourth plateau. All I know is I said: 'I'll go myself!' The action was automatic; I felt like I was watching someone else do things.
### Chapter 6

Gotō: I came to in a daze, and the first thing I did was log into Arena Breakout to farm Vincent — I really am a total Breakout junkie! Anyway, the second before I started farming, I felt a 'statistical high valley'.

Gotō: I went into a match and found: I could see people, but I couldn't immediately register 'that's a person!'; I could only cognize 'that's the shape of a person!'. Visual sharpness had dropped too, and people looked bigger — more precisely, my FOV had shrunk.

Gotō: after that I got out of bed feeling awful, with obvious motor enhancement. I drank a cup of hot tea, then threw up, and felt much better. The motor enhancement was strong enough that nothing I did tired me, and I could even jump repeatedly without tiring. Then the respiratory depression came, so I had to breathe in big gulps.
Included Remarks
Gotō: this report describes the effects of the fifth plateau, but I hope people will pay more attention to the adverse reactions.
Gotō: please don't follow my example.
Fill in the Gaps
Gotō: I'm crippled now; I suspect I broke my leg on the fifth plateau.

Gotō: fifth-plateau reactions: space — perception lost; vision — cognition weakened; time — perception lost; hallucinations with eyes open and closed; consciousness — falling into a 'trap'; memory — as if eroded, unclear; touch — dulled; hearing — pickup increased but not denoised; movement — performing a little psychosis theatre.
Gotō: since hearing, touch, vision and taste have been dissociated away leaving only hearing, I suggest listening to music to relieve the suffering of consciousness.
Handler's Note

No. 2 is the full version of RP-7-23 in report 7. The original contained the specific rounds and quantities; they have been blacked out. What's kept is the experience, the chapter structure, and the line 'please don't follow my example'.
